description: Shared correctness fixtures (docs/benchmark-correctness-fixtures.md). Every dataset generates a deterministic value stream; every variant reads that same stream and accumulates a checksum from it, regardless of how it allocates (reused, freshly-allocated-and-discarded, bursty, retained-and-growing). Allocation pattern and collector choice change GC pressure and pause behavior, never the checksum.

semantics.xorshift64: x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >>> 7 (unsigned/logical); x ^= x << 17 (64-bit wrapping, unsigned interpretation throughout)
semantics.objectGraphChurn: value[i] = i (linear, no RNG); extra payload = 8 longs/node
semantics.messagePipeline: value[i] = xorshift64 stream (seed=60) unsigned-mod 1000000; extra payload = 16 longs/node
semantics.retainedCache: value[i] = xorshift64 stream (seed=61) unsigned-mod 1000000; extra payload = 4 longs/node
semantics.lowAllocationReuse: a single node is allocated once and its value field mutated every iteration — near-zero allocation
semantics.steadyHighAllocation: a fresh node is allocated every iteration and discarded immediately after its value is read
semantics.burstyAllocation: iterations alternate in fixed blocks: 100 reused (as lowAllocationReuse) then 20 freshly-allocated with an 8x larger payload, repeating for the full n
semantics.growingLiveSet: a fresh node is allocated every iteration AND retained in a never-shrinking list — live set grows monotonically to n nodes by the end of the run
semantics.collectorMatrix: IDENTICAL code and allocation pattern to steadyHighAllocation; only the launching JVM's collector flag differs (G1 vs Parallel) — a runner-level distinction, not a code distinction
